title: Oliver Jackson and Eddie Locke; a break
summary: Jones recalls mentoring two young drummers and telling them what to expect, before a short break.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: we've had a hectic situation for 22 years. But we could never know, with all this wealth of talent out here - and we're not in a position, we don't travel around even though we got the airplane and everything - we're not in a position because we're not set in our views. We've gone into certain things. Like I'm with a drum shop for 2 years and my heart bleeds that I can't go out and give this. You know two little kids that stayed with me, Oliver Jackson and Eddie Locke. I used to tell them, "You're going to play with Earl Hines -"
Eddie Locke - he's a great drummer -

He's playing with Roy Budd Johnson thing. I used to sit down and tell them, "You're going to play with Earl Hines. You're going to play with Teddy Wilson. You're going to play with Dorothy Donegan. You're going to play with this. You're going to Newport. You're going to Europe." "I am?" I'd say, "Sure you are." "When?" I'd say, "You'll find out." So they found out. I had to tell them now, you see. You know how difficult it is to have a group that's going to stay together for 4 or 5 years, with economic situation as it is now and social conditions still as it is. But these guys they come out and they play.
Let's take a little break... and wet our throats a little here.
